newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-BRAVES, CARDINALS WIN, REACH NL CHAMPIONSHIP SERIES.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-BRAVES, CARDINALS WIN, REACH NL CHAMPIONSHIP SERIES.

text.p: The St louis Cardinals finished a sweep of the San Diego Padres on Saturday, and the Atlanta Braves beat the Los Angeles Dodgers to reach the National League Championship Series (NLCS).
Brian Jordan's two-run homer in the top of the ninth inning powered the Cardinals to a 7-5 victory and into their first NLCS in nine years, beginning Wednesday in Atlanta.

In Atlanta, the Braves jumped on Dodgers' starter Hideo Nomo for five runs, five hits and five walks in 3-2/3 innings. Nomo had dominated the Braves in three regular season starts, going 2-0 with a 1.61 ERA in 22-1/3 innings.
The Braves got 6-2/3 strong innings from Tom Glavine and a two-run homer from Chipper Jones to beat the Dodgers 5-2 to reach their fifth straight NLCS.
Atlanta hit five homers in the three games and held Los Angeles to just five runs.
"I was borderline," Glavine said, but "my changeup was good today."
Asked his reaction to reaching the NLCS again, he said: "I was surprised. The margin of error is very small."

The Padres, who blew a 4-1 lead, tied the game for the last time on Ken Caminiti's second homer of the game in the bottom of the eighth inning off Rick Honeycutt. But Jordan's blast sent Atlanta to a 3-0 whitewash of the Padres, who lost their sixth straight playoff series, dating to the 1984 World Series.
With one out, Ron Gant drew a walk and Jordan launched a homer to left off closer Trevor Hoffman (0-1), who usually does not pitch in tie games.

T.J. Mathews, the fourth Cardinals pitcher, came on after Caminiti's homer and went one scoreless inning. Dennis Eckersley worked the ninth for his third save of the series and 14th of his postseason career.
Jordan's RBI single in the first gave St. Louis the lead, but San Diego scored in three straight innings off Cardinals starter Donovan Osborne.
"I gave up the NFL for Baseball three years ago and this made that choice the right one," Jordan said. "This was the biggest game of my life. The Braves will be tough but we can play with them."
Cardinals' manager Tony LaRussa said: "Jordan made a great diving catch or they would have gone ahead in the 8th and then he hit it. He's a much better player than people know about."
Of losing three straight, Caminiti said, "Getting to the post season is so hard, it hurts to go out this easy."
